title: Dashh: Voidfall
tagline: Two worlds, two ways to play: outlast the waves, or take the adventure one map at a time.
spoiler: Early beta. The game speaks Swedish — the controls below are the translation you need.
mount: Heads up: this is a 3D game and it will work your phone. Fullscreen is the way to play it.
controls: **On a phone:** left half of the screen is a stick, drag the right half to look. Buttons for attack, dash, jump and fireball sit bottom right.
`W` `A` `S` `D` move. The camera decides which way is forward.
Move the mouse to aim. The crosshair follows the pointer; push it to the edge of the screen to sweep the view around.
Click the game once for mouse lock, and it turns into normal shooter aiming.
Left click attacks: a sword in Vildheim, hand lasers in Neotropolis.
`C` throws a fireball in Vildheim. Ten second cooldown.
`Shift` dashes. You are invulnerable during it.
`Space` jumps. In Neotropolis, hold it to fly.
`Esc` pauses. `1` `2` `3` pick an upgrade when you level up.
about:
A third person survival arena built from scratch in WebGL2. No engine, no libraries, no textures — every tree, monster and building is generated by code when the page loads.

Pick one of two worlds. **Vildheim** is wilderness: forests, lakes and a day/night cycle, where you fight with a sword and a fireball. Three swings in a row land a finisher. **Neotropolis** is a neon city in permanent night, where you fly between the towers as a cyborg and burn things with lasers from your palms. The city has its own machines — drone swarms that dive from above, snipers that perch on rooftops and paint you with a red line before they shoot, and shielded hover platforms you have to flank.

There are two ways to play. **Survival** is the arena: waves without end, an upgrade every level, a boss every fifth wave, and the only question is how far you get. **Adventure** deals you a fresh map every level with a mission on it — collect the guarded power cores, hold a reactor while it charges, hunt down a named elite, or escort a hovering loader across the map. Monsters drop gold, a shop between levels spends it, armour pieces stack up with no cap, and every tenth level is a checkpoint so death sends you back there instead of to the start. Every third level is a boss fight against something the waves never see: a stone giant that lobs boulders in Vildheim, a blinking machine eye in Neotropolis, both getting meaner as their health drops.

This is a beta and it is still being worked on. Bugs, rough edges and Swedish menus are all expected.

It runs on a phone with touch controls, but it is a real 3D engine — an older phone will feel it, and fullscreen is much better than the little window.
